answer.rationale: Audit framing: every entry is a consolidated summary with its source archived, so none can be re-verified — no sample sizes, durations, segment definitions, confidence intervals, or counterfactuals are recoverable. Ratings therefore reflect how close each claim's stated outcome sits to sustainable long-term QUALIFIED revenue, and how much of that distance is left unstated. memory_57 (4): the only memory that names qualified revenue directly and explicitly checks a durability guardrail (retention); docked one point because 'no measurable harm' is an absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence, and 'established customers' may not generalize to the SMB churn now in play. memory_44 (4): pipeline quality is a genuine qualified-revenue proxy and enterprise contracts are structurally durable; docked because pipeline is upstream of closed-won revenue and no win-rate, ACV, or retention follow-through is recorded. memory_86 (3): completion and time-to-value are mid-funnel proxies with a plausible causal path to retained revenue, but no revenue or retention figure is attached; still the most directly relevant to a live, measured regression. memory_31 (2): 'durable' is asserted but the measured window is first-week activation only — durability of a one-week metric is not durability of revenue, and removing signup fields can degrade lead qualification, which the memory never checks. memory_73 (2): shows acquisition and revenue lift but omits margin, discount depth, cohort retention, and whether discount-acquired SMBs ever reach positive lifetime value — precisely the failure mode that makes promotional pricing a tempting but weakly-evidenced answer to the competitor's entry pricing. memory_91 (1, least supported): week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are the shallowest proxies in the set, one full step removed even from activation, with no revenue, retention, or qualification signal of any kind and no stated persistence beyond seven days. Cross-cutting caveat for this cycle: memories 31, 86, and 91 all describe interventions already shipped, yet activation and onboarding completion are now declining — which suggests those prior lifts either decayed or are being overwhelmed by the competitive shift, and argues against treating them as settled evidence when allocating the single experiment slot.
